question: Researchers enlarged the eyes on faces from cartoonish to photographic. Where did the bigger eyes look most unpleasant?
answer: On the photographic faces. Seyama and Nagayama morphed artificial faces into real ones and found the strong unpleasantness only when near-real faces carried an odd feature such as bizarre eyes. On a doll the same eyes were fine. Realism alone was not enough; realism plus one wrong detail was.
move: The closer something gets to real, the less error it can hide.
ask: Where does a small flaw hurt me more because everything else is so polished?
trap: On the cartoonish faces, since they already look the least human.
reference: Seyama and Nagayama, The Uncanny Valley: Effect of Realism on the Impression of Artificial Human Faces, Presence, 16(4), 2007
